whatItDoes: fiber_sweep.py (Python 3 stdlib) re-derives Skyhook's finance/skyhook_finance.py chain from the workbook ladder and the rev_a.json excerpt, gates itself at $0/kg against 19 published anchors (the three workbook triples $8,741M/Y17/−$3,883M, $5,772M/Y9, $4,226M/Y7, the $6,877M/Y14 variant, and the five rev_a mass ratios and fiber masses), then adds the fiber PURCHASE line the model lacks (price × multiplier × fiber kg, spread 15/30/35/20 over Y1–4, no hardware mass factor) and sweeps it over $0–3,000/kg for the three columns and the two option tiers, recomputing all eight sensitivity.py thresholds and the fiber price at which each baseline single stops closing the case ($156 program capex, $314 launch, $1,210 derate, $12,822 cadence). `--quote P` prints a quote-day card (at $300/kg: conservative +$183M, $8,741M→$8,924M, Y17 unchanged, NPV −$3,883M→−$4,026M, launch threshold $1,674→$1,508; cislunar +$443M; Phase 3 +$4,629M); bare `--quote` exits 2 because rev_a's key is null, and no fiber line prints without a price. index.html runs the same chain in JS (model.js, own erf) reconciled to the Python output, with a structured refusal, marker chips labelled "not a quote", gate table, two width-aware charts and tables.

(2) rev_a.json itself: the five mass ratios/fiber masses to the printed decimals, and the cislunar block's own 686 (launch breakeven) and 517 (price breakeven) reproduced from the chain (686.26 / 516.73). (4) Closed forms: launch-threshold slope −m/hmf, price threshold = Y15 breakeven, single stop price = cum15(0)·1000/(fiber_t·m), all-zero cash flow never pays back. (5) A run of the live module (tier ladder $12,644M/Y22/−$6,946M, $75,434M/>Y40/−$56,176M) and, when the checkout + openpyxl are present, the imported finance.skyhook_finance to 1e-9 (ran and passed here). (6) Round trips: reference.json == fresh `--json --quote 300`; example.txt blocks re-run identically; model.js reconciled to reference.json (>350 numbers, 1e-9/1e-6); the page's card lines equal the CLI's card lines (ui-check runs the CLI). deviationsFromProposal: Added an index.html (the proposal was CLI-only; the brief allows a page where it adds value) with a JS port reconciled to the Python output rather than a second model. Eight thresholds, not six: all of sensitivity.py's INPUTS, matching the FINDINGS table. The sweep grid is a half-decade log grid 0/10/30/100/300/1000/3000 (the charts use 49 points), not a dense log sweep. A third marker was added (the strategy simulator's $250 [Speculative]) beside MP-001 and inspace_fork's $1,000. The $0 gate was widened from the three triples to 19 anchors (variant + five rev_a ratios/masses); thresholds and the rev_a 686/517 are pinned in tests rather than in the gate. Thresholds on a base case that already closes (option tiers) are reported as the base value, a convention not in sensitivity.py, stated in the README. ladder.json is 4 KB, not 1 KB, because it keeps column A labels and column E source notes. The proposal's cited citations all verified (rev_a null + note, README.md:80, DECISION_LOG.md:60 item 8, MORNING_REPORT.md:48 anomaly 5, handoff.md:37-38, MP-001 line 24, inspace_fork.py:55 and :194, jsx:54); none was dropped. NPV@8/12% are in the JSON only.
notBuilt: No yarn-to-finished-tether conversion: the multiplier is a knob with no source anywhere in the checkouts, so it defaults to 1.0 and is labelled unsourced rather than given an invented value. Volume pricing is not modelled: the vendor ask was a 1 t/100 t/600 t ladder and the script takes one price per run. Fiber replacement cadence (DECISION_LOG item 10, creep) is unmodelled; it would make fiber an opex line too. Option-tier rows are the canonical module's partial tier model (only tip speed changes), not a cislunar business case. Skyhook's pytest suite was not run (pytest is not installed here); the mirror was verified by importing finance.skyhook_finance instead. The JS erf is my own, checked at ten tabulated points, not proven. The page's charts are checked by counts and text, not pixels. Not through Skyhook's Rule 1 canon review, a verification memo, or the pytest suite; the workbook ladder read is the human-review-pending one the module itself reads.
